Imagine you are in a long line of people and want to know how many are ahead of you, so you ask the person in front of you to ask the person in front of them, and so on. Eventually, the question reaches the very first person in line, who simply replies "zero" because no one is ahead of them. This answer is then passed back down the line, with each person adding one to the total until it finally reaches you. In programming, recursion works the exact same way: a function solves a problem by calling a smaller version of itself until it hits a simple base case, and then builds the final answer on the way back out.
